# Torsion bar adjustment and ride height

> **[Unverified]** This page rests on a single community report. Cross-check before relying on it.

> Items marked **[Partial]** are only partly confirmed by the source and need more work. They stay in the review queue and are firmed up, corrected or removed as more sources come in.

## Summary

[Partial] Turn down the front end by turning the torsion bars to adjust the setting and lower or raise the ride height as needed. [t1774]

## Procedure

> **[Partial]** Needs more work: the verifier could confirm only part of this procedure (the steps marked [Partial], or whether the list is complete). Steps or precautions may be wrong or missing; read the source thread before relying on it. Later runs fill it in as more sources are found.

1. Turn down the front end by turning the torsion bars.
2. [Partial] Adjust the setting to lower or raise the ride height as needed.

_Procedure reported by [t1774]._

## Tips & gotchas

- Reindexing helps level the ride and center travel of the bars. [t1774]
- Use a chalk test on tires: draw a line across with driveway chalk, roll it on the ground several times to check wear patterns. If chalk remains on outside lugs, tire pressure is too high. [t1774]

## Common mistakes

- [Partial] Cranking torsion bars too much without checking bump clearance. [t1774]
- Running excessive tire pressure (50+ psi) which causes a rough ride quality. [t1774]
